hypothesis: Without a heat file the CUDA tier's warm start fills the card in index order, whole layers: on a T4 holding 6605 of 10240 experts layers 0-24 sit on the card and layers 26-39 hold none, so a prompt chunk copies all of each later layer's experts over the bus after running 25 layers with the bus idle (by construction; no bus timeline was taken). Taking expert 0 of every layer, then expert 1, makes every layer copy its share beside the work of the layer before, and the 512-token prompt that follows a 64-token one and its 32 decode steps is faster.
command: bench.c built against c/ (cd c && make <objects> CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_75, as the record's setup); COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPUS=0 CUDA_EXPERT_GB=auto OMP_WAIT_POLICY=ACTIVE OMP_PROC_BIND=close ./qwen36-bench --model <model> --text promessi_sposi.txt --lengths 64,512 --gen 32 --teacher

hardware.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.00GHz (4 cores / 8 threads) + NVIDIA Tesla T4 (15360 MiB, sm_75, up to PCIe Gen3 x16)
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Google Colab, T4 high-RAM), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07

config.scenario: the 512-token prompt after a 64-token prompt and its 32 decode steps, one process
config.tok_s: prompt tokens / the prompt's seconds (bench's prefill_tps of the 512 row)

quality.method: make -C c check (macOS arm64), 2763 tests; on the T4 and on the RTX 3070 with the code measured make -C c cuda-test, cuda-chain-check, tests/test_qwen36_cuda_chain and the tier tests pass. The PR without a heat file gives the bits of dev with a heat file in the same order (correctness.txt: 64 and 512 tokens on both cards); the same prompts and teacher-forced answers in every run of both versions; the experts moved to the card run on its kernels instead of the CPU's, so the logits of a conversation move in the last digits
